title: Send JMAP chairs request for 2 min AOB slot at IETF 127 + one-slide outline (drafted, not sent)
description:
Ask the JMAP chairs for about 2 minutes in AOB at IETF 127 (Thu 2026-11-19 09:00-10:30 PST, Golden Gate 1) for draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00, ideally next to the "JMAP account settings" item. Mark is remote. Drafted 2026-11-15. NOT SENT; needs Mark's explicit approval. Send as soon as approved, before the list email if need be; the chairs need time to fit a remote presenter in.

Chairs: Bron Gondwana <brong@fastmailteam.com>, Jim Fenton <fenton@bluepopcorn.net>. Responsible AD: Andy Newton (not cc'd).

---------------------------------------------------------------------
From: Mark Atwood <mark@reviewcommit.com>
To: jmap-chairs@ietf.org
Subject: IETF 127 JMAP: 2 minutes in AOB for draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00?

Hi Bron, Jim,

I've written draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00. It adds localized display
text to the existing JMAP data types and updates RFC 8620 on text
handling, URIs (RFC 3986) and problem details (RFC 9457). I'm posting
it to the list this week:

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-atwood-jmap-updates/

Could I have about 2 minutes in AOB on Thursday, with one slide? It
fits best next to the account settings item, since the draft defines
an account-level language preference that may belong in that work.
I'll be remote.

If the agenda is too tight, no problem: I'll queue at the mic during
the account settings discussion, or just leave it to the list.

Thanks,
Mark

---------------------------------------------------------------------
ONE-SLIDE OUTLINE (for the chairs' slide deck, if a slot is granted)

Title: draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00: i18n, URIs, problem details

- Gap: display text (Mailbox, AddressBook, Calendar, Principal and
  Quota names and descriptions) has one value and no language.
- Fix: optional capability urn:ietf:params:jmap:i18n adds JSCalendar
  `locale` and `localizations`, plus a `language` argument on
  /get, /query and /queryChanges (RFC 4647 Lookup).
- Accept-Language never changes /get data, so caches stay coherent.
  Updates RFC 9425 for opt-in clients.
- Account `preferredLanguages`, for text written with no request in
  progress. Overlaps account settings: happy to move it there.
- For all of JMAP, at SHOULD level: text profiles, no server
  normalization, truncation on grapheme boundaries, RFC 3986 URIs,
  RFC 9457 problem details from every HTTP resource.
- Ask: WG interest? Split parts into an RFC 8620bis?

Speaker note (two minutes): name the gap, say "one draft, opt-in
capability plus SHOULD-level updates", call out the overlap with
account settings, and ask the two questions. Point to the list thread.
